function: Two-tier hierarchical sparse autoencoder for CSI compression and feedback, with learned Bernoulli-Laplace-mixture prior and fixed-length adaptive range coding (pp. 1-2, 4-7).
system: Downlink FDD MIMO-OFDM, 32-antenna ULA BS, single-antenna UE, 1024 subcarriers, 32 delays; COST 2100 indoor 5.3 GHz and outdoor 300 MHz bands; no RIS (pp. 3, 11).
method: Two-tier convolutional autoencoder trained unsupervised with variational-Bayes rate-distortion loss (Bernoulli-Laplace-mixture prior); one common model for both scenarios; weights initialized across budgets by transfer learning (pp. 4-12).
data_channel: COST 2100 indoor (5.3 GHz) and outdoor (300 MHz) public benchmark datasets: 100,000 training samples each, 30,000 validation and 20,000 test per scenario (p. 11).
test_conditions: One common model trained on mixed indoor and outdoor data; tested per scenario on held-out samples of the same COST 2100 data, five feedback budgets (p. 11).
baselines: CsiNet+, CRNet, TransNet, CSI-StripeFormer, DeepCMC+, CsiVBA, all learned autoencoders; no classical codebook or compressed-sensing baseline in the results (pp. 12-13).
metrics: NMSE (dB) and cosine distance versus feedback budget in bits per pixel (BPP 3/16 to 3), indoor and outdoor; parameters and FLOPs (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Table II: proposed 61.76 K learnable parameters and 122.74 M FLOPs for online inference, listed beside six baselines (p. 13).
openness: none; no code or data link, trains on public COST 2100 benchmark datasets of prior works (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 11: "Two types of channel matrices are generated through the COST 2100 channel model [35]", indoor at 5.3 GHz and outdoor at 300 MHz, used for training and testing.
q2_support: p. 11: "The training dataset contains 100,000 indoor channel realizations and 100,000 outdoor channel realizations" and "the validation and testing for different scenarios are performed separately", so both scenarios are seen in training and tests use held-out samples; p. 12: "The hyper-parameter configurations for P(A-3) corresponding to different feedback budgets are presented in Table I", each budget is trained separately. No unseen scenario, band or antenna count is tested.
q3_support: p. 12: "We compare the proposed CSI feedback scheme against four baseline schemes" and lists six, all neural autoencoders (CsiNet+, CRNet, TransNet, CSI-StripeFormer, DeepCMC+, CsiVBA); p. 1: "codebook-based [4], [5], [6], [7] and sparse-compression-based" methods are only named, never evaluated. No non-learned baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 13: "the complexities of different CSI feedback schemes are compared in Table II based on the number of learnable parameters"; Table II (p. 13) gives the proposed scheme 61.76 K parameters and 122.74 M FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 11: "we utilize the public benchmark datasets employed in many existing works" (COST 2100 indoor and outdoor channels); no link to its own code or data.
notes: Page 1 shows the title and DOI 10.1109/TSP.2024.3423660. Area 2: CSI compression and feedback. q2 is 0 because both scenarios are in the training set and the test sets are held-out samples of them, and each feedback budget is trained on its own. q3 is 0 because all six baselines are learned (the text says four but lists six, p. 12); the greedy element dropping of Fig. 5(a), p. 3, only illustrates sparsity and is not compared with the proposed scheme. q5 is 1 only through the public benchmark COST 2100 datasets, with no code release. CSI is assumed perfectly known at the UE (p. 4, footnote 1). The text gives the outdoor scenario as semi-urban on p. 3 and rural on p. 11.
